## Decisions

- OpenGeo starts with user intent, not system inventory: New map, Open a file, Open a project, and Recent projects are primary. Familiar GIS menus, Layers/ Browser docks, inspectors, plugins, and governed administration remain fully available through progressive disclosure. A new blank browser map is never allowed to overwrite an existing authoritative map implicitly.

- OpenGeo has two production origins. `https://opengeo.tools` is anonymous compiled publication output; `https://studio.opengeo.tools` is the authenticated GIS/source/publication-control application and the same-origin API boundary. The existing public library must be preserved while its complete recovered source is imported privately and its rights inventory is completed.

- Public classification is necessary but insufficient for release. Public pages and maps require a reviewed permissive license and attribution, while private ownership is bound to Cognito subject and PostgreSQL membership rather than display name or email inference.

- PostgreSQL/PostGIS replaces the prototype's proposed DynamoDB metadata store for production authoritative records.

- OpenGeo must be standalone-capable while treating GeoLibre, GeoNode, GeoMoose, GeoServer, MapServer, and OpenLayers as separately measured optional peers, clients, renderers, or migration references. None is a required runtime dependency for standalone parity acceptance.

- Modern OGC APIs are canonical; WMS/WFS/WMTS/WCS and selected CSW/WPS behavior are compatibility facades over the same governed data, metadata, styles, and permissions.

- “Project publishing” means general multi-page sites with mixed content, editorial state, maps, print output, and portable static export—not only a public map route.

- S3 remains the object/derivative store.

- Physical S3 names are human-readable and role-based: `opengeo.tools` is public publication output, `studio.opengeo.tools` is the private Studio web origin, `source.opengeo.tools` is private source/build storage, and `storage.opengeo.tools` is private managed GIS data storage. Environment words are readable leading labels rather than generated numeric suffixes. Regional path-style S3 HTTPS avoids dotted-bucket wildcard-certificate failures; database credentials live in Secrets Manager, never S3.

- An external database connection is not a managed dataset. Reference remains externally authoritative and creates no OpenGeo-owned bytes; an explicit snapshot creates a separate managed version with exact `derived_from` lineage. Initial database access is server-mediated and read-only.

- Markdown is the default page-authoring source, compiled to bounded declarative OpenGeo blocks. Untrusted Observable JavaScript never runs on the authenticated origin; full Framework compilation requires an isolated worker and separate preview origin.

- The Observable app is retained as a UX prototype while the production API and shared domain contracts are built; replacement is incremental.

- Lambda HTTP API is the default request-driven API; ECS/Fargate remains an explicit transitional API and a candidate only for on-demand heavyweight GIS execution. EKS is not the default platform.

- Optimistic locking precedes CRDT work.

- The default API has no VPC attachment and reaches Aurora through Data API; it has bounded reserved concurrency and no provisioned concurrency. The old public-subnet/ALB task is an explicit transitional dev-only exception. GIS workers use isolated subnets and exact private endpoints only while their separate activation stack exists.

- The GIS parser stays in the reviewed no-public/default-egress Fargate boundary. Its whole conditional stack is activated only for bounded processing windows and removed afterward; scaling tasks to zero alone is not an inactive state. Lifecycle automation follows only after exact-stack deletion and race/rollback controls are proven.

- API and worker database credentials are distinct from each other and from migration/recovery credentials; the worker has function-only authority.

- Each environment uses a dedicated AWS account and an account-wide monitored budget so untaggable networking/data-transfer spend remains visible.
